sources.title: Comparing the Framing Effect in Humans and LLMs on Naturally Occurring Texts
sources.paper_license: ACL Anthology states post-2016 ACL materials are CC BY 4.0; this applies to the paper publication, not automatically to underlying source texts or human response data.
sources.notes: The Anthology page identifies the paper, abstract and PDF but does not itself identify a dataset-specific license, consent notice, raw-data repository or human-response data-use terms. The source describes 1,000 naturally occurring texts and human sentiment annotations. No raw text or participant-level records were downloaded or committed.

sources.title: Agreement Helps, Disagreement Matters: Scaling Framing Function Annotation With Large Language Models
sources.paper_license: Article page is marked open access; the article-page statement does not establish rights for underlying social-media posts or annotation records.
sources.notes: The reported study annotates 455 EV-related social-media posts with three human coders. Raw posts, author metadata, annotation payloads and codebook artifacts are not admitted until their specific rights, deletion/retention and data-use conditions are reviewed.

sources.title: AI Agents Are Sensitive to Nudges
sources.paper_license: PMC reports the article is CC BY 4.0; supplementary data/code rights and human-reference data terms require their own review.
sources.notes: Use as a methodology and behavioral-choice comparator only. Do not ingest human-level trial records, supplements or model outputs until artifact provenance and their separate terms are checked.

sources.title: AfriSenti multilingual sentiment dataset
sources.paper_license: Dataset card reports CC-BY-NC-SA-2.0; confirm exact snapshot, source-content restrictions and allowed derivative use before any payload access.
sources.notes: Sentiment labels are not framing-function annotations or semantic-equivalence judgments. Its reported 14-language list is not the target five-language South African scope; do not treat it as a substitute or repurpose labels as framing ground truth.

sources.title: MasakhaNEWS African-language news topic dataset
sources.paper_license: Dataset-card licensing metadata is not internally consistent across the surfaced card views (AFL-3.0 badge and CC/non-commercial wording); resolve exact revision and provenance before use.
sources.notes: Topic classification is not framing annotation. The inspected card includes isiXhosa but not the full requested target set. Do not use the corpus or its labels as framing ground truth.

sources.title: Linguistically annotated dataset for four official South African languages with a conjunctive orthography
sources.paper_license: Article reports open-access Creative Commons licensing; the underlying corpus's exact Seanoe data license and allowed derivative/annotation terms require direct verification.
sources.notes: Resource covers isiNdebele, isiXhosa, isiZulu and Siswati and linguistic layers such as morphology, POS and lemmas. It is not a framing or deliberation dataset and does not supply human framing judgments.

sources.title: SA-Knowledge South African language resources
sources.paper_license: Dataset card identifies thesis-linked subsets and source scope; exact license and permitted use must be resolved per subset.
sources.notes: Card lists isiZulu, isiXhosa, Sepedi, Sesotho and English and government-domain subsets. It does not provide framing-function labels. Rights must be assessed independently per subset before use.
